surprises: Amending the sort acceptance to a fixed per-column direction left the one sortable header inert - changeQuerySort re-sets sortBy to the default "name", so the control can never change state.
All three gates and the sort test passed over that inert control because the test only asserted aria-sort at rest and never clicked the header.
Deduping the athletes filter helper onto useListFormatters().compact silently changed athletes' option counts (12500 now renders "12.5K", previously "13K") with no test covering it.

proposed_rules.diff: - **Do not ship a control whose handler cannot change state.** When the contract cannot serve an affordance - a sort with no `sortDirection`, a toggle with no inverse - remove the affordance and land the contract phase first; rendering it inert reads as broken and announces a state that never moves. A test for an interactive control must actuate it and assert the state changed; asserting only its rest state (`aria-sort` before any click) passes on a control wired to nothing.

- **Consolidating two formatters onto one owner is a behavior change until the resolved options match.** `Intl` defaults are not the same as an explicit option bag - compact defaults round 12500 to "13K" while `maximumFractionDigits: 1` yields "12.5K". Diff the resolved options at every call site the dedupe touches, and cover the changed output with a test or keep the original bag; a helper dedupe that quietly reformats numbers on an untouched page is not a refactor.

- **A constant that a second module must match is exported and imported, never restated.** A skeleton that hard-codes `miw={280}` beside siblings that import their widths drifts from the real column the first time the column changes, and nothing fails. If a literal must agree across files, it has exactly one exported owner.
